title: [PDF] Letter from the Governor to Baroness Noakes DBE
summary: Andrew Bailey, Governor of the Bank of England, has responded to the House of Lords Financial Services Regulation Committee's report on private markets, announcing the launch of a Private Markets System-Wide Exploratory Scenario (PM SWES) to test how the private markets ecosystem might respond under stress. The letter confirms UK banks have £173bn in banking book exposures to private market funds and leveraged corporates, equivalent to 8% of wholesale portfolios. The FPC also adjusted its benchmark for system-wide Tier 1 capital requirements to around 13% of risk-weighted assets.
key_points: The Bank of England's Financial Policy Committee (FPC) is launching a Private Markets System-Wide Exploratory Scenario (PM SWES) to test private market resilience at current scale, with Round 1 results expected in 2026 and a final report in early 2027
Major participants including alternative asset managers, banks, insurers, pension funds, and endowments have joined the exercise, including firms headquartered outside the UK

UK banks collectively hold £173bn in banking book exposures to private market funds and leveraged corporates backed by finance sponsors, representing 8% of total committed limits across wholesale portfolios
The FPC has lowered its benchmark for system-wide Tier 1 capital requirements from 14% to approximately 13% of risk-weighted assets, citing banks becoming less systemic and improved risk measurement
The Bank acknowledges private markets have not been tested by macroeconomic stress at their current scale
The PRA conducted a 2024 thematic review of private-equity-related financing activities and has received bank responses on risk management of PE exposures
why_it_matters: This letter signals that UK regulators view private markets as a potential systemic risk requiring targeted stress testing. The £173bn exposure figure quantifies the banking system's interconnection with private markets, while the PM SWES exercise indicates regulators are proactively building understanding before a stress event. The capital requirement adjustment to around 13% suggests the FPC views current bank resilience as adequate, but the private market focus signals ongoing monitoring priorities.
macro_context: Private markets have grown significantly in the UK over two decades without testing by macroeconomic stress at current size. The FPC views private finance as essential for supporting growth and productive investment, but acknowledges systemic risks require monitoring as the sector evolves, including funded reinsurance and AI sector growth.
market_structure_context: The PM SWES exercise will examine complex interconnections within the private markets ecosystem, including alternative asset managers, public market-focused managers, private equity and credit funds, banks, insurers, pension funds, endowments, and foundations. Data gaps remain a concern for effective monitoring. The letter notes many participants are headquartered outside the UK, reflecting the global nature of the sector.
important_numbers: £173bn - UK banks' banking book exposures to private market funds and leveraged corporates
8% - equivalent to total committed limits across wholesale portfolios
13% - revised FPC benchmark for system-wide Tier 1 capital requirements (down from 14%)
2026 - expected completion of firm engagement and analysis for PM SWES
early 2027 - planned publication of final PM SWES report
